questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 5]

Let f(x) = ln x − 5x, for x > 0.
(a) Find f′(x). [2]
(b) Find f″(x). [1]
(c) Solve f′(x) = f″(x). [2]

2. [Maximum mark: 6]

A biased four-sided die is rolled.

[Table: Score: 1, 2, 3, 4. Probability: 0.28, k, 0.15, 0.3.]
(a) Find k. [2]
(b) Calculate the expected value. [2]
(c) The die is rolled 80 times. On how many rolls would you expect to obtain a three? [2]

3. [Maximum mark: 6]

A circle has centre O and radius 4 cm. Points A and B lie on it and AÔB=θ, where 0≤θ≤π.

[Diagram not to scale: The minor circular segment between chord AB and arc AB is shaded.]
(a) Find the area of the shaded region, in terms of θ. [3]
(b) The area is 12 cm². Find θ. [3]
questions.solution: (a) Area=8θ−8sinθ=8(θ−sinθ). (b) Solve 8(θ−sinθ)=12 to get θ=2.27 radians.

Let g(x)=−(x−1)²+5.
(a) Write down the vertex. [1]
Let f(x)=x². [Diagram: graph y=x² on a coordinate grid.] The graphs intersect at x=−1 and x=2.

5. [Maximum mark: 6]

P(A)=0.62 and P(A∩B)=0.18.
(a) Find P(A∩B′). [2]
(b) Given P((A∪B)′)=0.19, find P(A|B′). [4]

6. [Maximum mark: 7]

Triangle ABC has a=8.1 cm, b=12.3 cm and area 15 cm². Find the largest possible perimeter.
questions.solution: sinC=30/(8.1·12.3). Use the obtuse C=162.475° for the larger third side. Cosine rule gives c=20.1720, so perimeter=40.6 cm.

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 8]

Let f(x)=e^(2sin(πx/2)), for x>0. The kth maximum point on the graph of f has x-coordinate xₖ, where k∈ℤ⁺.

(a) Given that xₖ₊₁=xₖ+a, find a. [4]

(b) Hence find the value of n such that ∑(from k=1 to n)xₖ=861. [4]
questions.summary: Use periodic maxima and a series.
questions.solution: Because the exponential function is increasing, f is greatest whenever sin(πx/2)=1. Thus πx/2=π/2+2πm, so x=1+4m. Hence x₁=1, x₂=5 and (a) a=4. (b) The xₖ form an arithmetic sequence with xₖ=1+4(k−1). Therefore 861=∑ₖ₌₁ⁿxₖ=n[2+4(n−1)]/2=n(2n−1). Solving 2n²−n−861=0 gives (2n+41)(n−21)=0; since n∈ℤ⁺, n=21.

8. [Maximum mark: 13]

[Table: ln x: 1.10, 2.08, 4.30, 6.03; ln y: 5.63, 5.22, 4.18, 3.41.]
The model is ln y=a ln x+b.
(a) Find a and b. [3]
(b) Estimate y when x=3.57. [3]
The relationship is also y=kxⁿ.
(c) By expressing ln y in terms of ln x, find n and k. [7]
questions.solution: (a) Regression gives a=−0.454,b=6.14. (b) ln y=5.56484, so y=261. (c) ln y=lnk+nlnx, hence n=−0.454 and k=e^6.14210=465.

9. [Maximum mark: 17]

Orange weights W are normal with mean 297 g. P(W>289)=0.79 and P(W>310)=0.095.
(a) Find P(289<W<310). [2]
The standard deviation is σ.
(b) (i) Find the standardized value for 289 g. (ii) Hence find σ. [5]
A grocer buys oranges exceeding the 35th percentile.
(c) To the nearest gram, find the minimum weight bought. [3]
Boxes contain 36 oranges.
(d) Find the probability the grocer buys more than half in a random box. [5]
(e) For two boxes, find the probability this happens in each. [2]

10. [Maximum mark: 15]

Let f(x)=12cosx−5sinx, −π≤x≤2π, with f(x)=f(x+2π). [Diagram: sinusoid with maximum A slightly left of the y-axis.] The minimum value is −13.
(a) Find A. [2]
(b) Write down (i) amplitude; (ii) period. [2]
(c) Hence write f(x)=p cos(x+r). [3]
A ball on a spring has distance d(t)=f(t)+17 cm from O, 0≤t≤5. [Diagram not to scale: ball hanging below O, distance d.]
(d) Find maximum speed. [3]
(e) Find the first time when speed is changing at 2 cm s⁻². [5]
questions.solution: (a) A=(−0.395,13). (b)(i) The amplitude is 13. (ii) The period is 2π. (c) Since 12=13cos r and 5=13sin r, r=tan⁻¹(5/12)=0.395, so f(x)=13cos(x+0.395). (d) d′(t)=−12sin t−5cos t=−13sin(t+0.395), so the maximum speed is max|d′(t)|=13 cm s⁻¹. (e) At the first required time the velocity is negative, so speed is −d′(t) and its rate of change is −d″(t). Set −d″(t)=2, where d″(t)=−12cos t+5sin t. Thus 12cos t−5sin t=2; the first solution on 0≤t≤5 is t=1.02 s.
